thesis: David Barron and Kazuhiko Shibata describe Symphony Financial Partners as a 20-year-old Asia-based manager of $1.3 billion in assets that focuses on deeply undervalued companies in Japan using a long-bias, constructive engagement strategy. They explain that their approach involves working closely with willing management teams to see intrinsic value reflected in the share price, addressing the disconnect between corporate activity and share price caused by Japan's employee-first, shareholder-last culture.
